entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2326-hx7g-3m9r: Apache MINA SSHD: integrity check bypass
entry.content:
Apache MINA SSHD: integrity check bypass

Aliases: CVE-2024-41909

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • org.apache.sshd:sshd-common — fixed in 2.12.0

Like many other SSH implementations, Apache MINA SSHD suffered from the issue that is more widely known as CVE-2023-48795. An attacker that can intercept traffic between client and server could drop certain packets from the stream, potentially causing client and server to consequently end up with a connection for which some security features have been downgraded or disabled, aka a Terrapin attack The mitigations to prevent this type of attack were implemented in Apache MINA SSHD 2.12.0, both client and server side. Users are recommended to upgrade to at least this version. Note that both the client and the server implementation must have mitigations applied against this issue, otherwise the connection may still be affected.

GeoServer has a Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) vulnerability in processing FreeMarker templates

Aliases: CVE-2024-45747

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-6w3v-mcfh-m3q7: Keycloak Admin UI REST Extensions: bulk role-removal endpoints fail to perform granular permission checks
entry.content:
Keycloak Admin UI REST Extensions: bulk role-removal endpoints fail to perform granular permission checks

Aliases: CVE-2026-11986

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-rest-admin-ui-ext — fixed in 26.7.0

A flaw was found in the admin-ui-ext component of Keycloak, which provides extended administrative user interface capabilities. The issue occurs because certain bulk role-removal endpoints fail to perform granular permission checks when deleting role mappings. This allows a delegated administrator with limited permissions to remove highly privileged roles from other users or groups, potentially disrupting administrative access control.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-45ph-gxxr-gwgw: XWiki Platform Live Data Live Table Connector has privilege escalation from edit to script right through Live Data editing
entry.content:
XWiki Platform Live Data Live Table Connector has privilege escalation from edit to script right through Live Data editing

Aliases: CVE-2026-53966

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • org.xwiki.platform:xwiki-platform-livedata-livetable — fixed in 16.10.17
  • org.xwiki.platform:xwiki-platform-livedata-livetable — fixed in 17.4.10
  • org.xwiki.platform:xwiki-platform-livedata-livetable — fixed in 17.10.4
  • org.xwiki.platform:xwiki-platform-livedata-livetable — fixed in 18.1.0-rc-1

### Impact Any user who can edit a page in XWiki can use Live Data's edit REST API in XWiki to change the rights on that page. This allows the user to obtain script right on the page. Script right allows the user to execute potentially dangerous Velocity scripts and send unfiltered HTML and JavaScript to the client. If there are other security checks, e.g., in extensions, implemented as listeners to `UserUpdatingDocumentEvent` and similar `User…` events, these checks can be circumvented, too. ### Patches This vulnerability has been patched by properly calling all checks in Live Data in XWiki 16.10.17, 17.4.10, 17.10.4 and 18.1.0. ### Workarounds We're not aware of any workarounds apart from upgrading.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-68mj-5wr7-6fgg: RabbitMQ Java client ValueReader: Oversized LongString/bytes length triggers OOM via unchecked allocation
entry.content:
RabbitMQ Java client ValueReader: Oversized LongString/bytes length triggers OOM via unchecked allocation

Aliases: CVE-2026-69219

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • com.rabbitmq:amqp-client — fixed in 5.33.1

## Summary `ValueReader.readBytes()` allocates a byte array sized by a wire-declared content length without validating it against actual frame data. A malicious AMQP peer triggers OOM by declaring a ~2GB string/bytes field. ## Vulnerable Code `src/main/java/com/rabbitmq/client/impl/ValueReader.java` lines 83-95: ```java private static byte[] readBytes(final DataInputStream in) throws IOException { final long contentLength = unsignedExtend(in.readInt()); if(contentLength < Integer.MAX_VALUE) { final byte[] buffer = new byte[(int)contentLength]; // allocates before reading in.readFully(buffer); return buffer; } } ``` ## Attack Scenario A malicious AMQP server sends a LongString field (type tag 'S') with declared length `0x7FFFFFFE` (2,147,483,646). …

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-5xwg-cfvj-gff5: RabbitMQ Java client accepts broker frames larger than the negotiated AMQP frame_max
entry.content:
RabbitMQ Java client accepts broker frames larger than the negotiated AMQP frame_max

Aliases: CVE-2026-61634

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • com.rabbitmq:amqp-client — fixed in 5.33.0

## Summary The max body size was enforced to patch CVE-2023-46120, but even though that limit still works, the frame size itself still exceeds the given max size. ## Root cause The Java client records the AMQP 0-9-1 `frame_max` negotiated during connection tuning, but the socket inbound frame reader continues to validate broker-controlled payload lengths against the much larger `maxInboundMessageBodySize` limit. A broker peer can therefore send a method frame whose payload is larger than the negotiated `frame_max`, have it allocated and decoded, and complete the connection handshake instead of being rejected as a protocol violation. *Reported by Team Atlanta.*

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-pq65-77rc-7r8c: Keycloak has a Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition
entry.content:
Keycloak has a Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition

Aliases: CVE-2026-9796

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • org.keycloak:keycloak-server — fixed in 26.6.4

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated administrator with the `manage-clients` role can exploit a Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerability in the name-based admin role checks. This allows the attacker to escalate their privileges to `realm-admin` for all users within the realm, granting them extensive control over the system. The composite role relationship persists even after the attacker's own permissions are revoked and across system reboots.

Netty: Memory Exhaustion in SctpMessageCompletionHandler

Aliases: CVE-2026-59902

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

  • io.netty:netty-transport-sctp — fixed in 4.1.137.Final

### Summary SctpMessageCompletionHandler does not limit the total size of buffered fragments, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to cause an OutOfMemoryError by sending large SCTP fragments. ### Details `io.netty.handler.codec.sctp.SctpMessageCompletionHandler` buffers fragments for incomplete SCTP messages. The fix for CVE-2026-46340 fixed unbounded memory growth by introducing limits on the number of concurrent incomplete messages (maxIncompleteSctpMessages) and the number of fragments per message (maxFragments). While the count of fragments is now bounded, the handler still does not enforce a maximum size in bytes. With the default limits of 128 messages and 128 fragments, and a typical max SCTP chunk size of 64KB, an attacker can consume up to ~1GB per connection. By opening a sma…

entry.content:
Apache cxf-core: No restriction on attachment headers per message

Aliases: CVE-2026-50645

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • org.apache.cxf:cxf-core — fixed in 4.2.2
  • org.apache.cxf:cxf-core — fixed in 4.1.7
  • org.apache.cxf:cxf-core — fixed in 3.6.12

There is no restriction on the amount of attachment headers that a message can contain when being deserialized by Apache CXF, which can lead to uncontrolled resource consumption or a denial of service attack. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.2.2 or 4.1.7 or 3.6.12, which fix this issue by imposing a maximum default of 500 attachments per message.
